Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma

HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 80 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 4550 of 2022 Applicant :- Rohit Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Vinod Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vikrant Gupta Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State.

The present anticipatory bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.75 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 494 IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Swar, Rampur.
Facts in brief are that in this case applicant is husband of the informant who was his wedded wife.
There was demand of dowry and harassment of the informant by this applicant and other members of his family.
She was ousted by the applicant from her marital house after ill-treatment.
The applicant has also entered into marriage with some other lady, though his first wife is alive.
After investigation charge-sheet has been submitted.

sentences.text: It is submitted that applicant is a bank employee and has committed no offence but this F.I.R. has been lodged with false allegation by the wife against the applicant while involving two other members of his family.
It is also submitted that proceeding under Section 494 IPC cannot be initiated only on the basis of police report but it can be done on the basis of complaint made by the aggrieved person.

It is also submitted that during investigation, applicant was granted interim relief and now after submission of charge-sheet process has been issued by the learned court therefore in pursuance of process of the court there is apprehension of arrest against the applicant so requested for anticipatory bail during trial.

It is also submitted that the informant has filed a petition under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act, in which she herself requested the court to direct the applicant not to make any interference with her.
He further submitted that charge-sheet has also been submitted under Section 494 Cr.P.C. in which cognizance cannot be taken by the lower court.
It is also submitted that the incident said to have taken place on 13.06.2019 regarding enticement of cousin of the informant was found to be false during investigation.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and urged that in this case applicant being husband of the informant has maltreated her and subjected her to harassment on account of non-fulfilment of demand of dowry, even during the wedlock he enticed the cousin of the informant and later on entered into marriage with her while informant (wedded wife) was alive regarding which a case was also registered by father of the victim.
After investigation, the offences were found prima facie established as a result charge-sheet was submitted against the applicant.

Further urged that the offences said to have been committed by the applicant are punishable with sentence less than seven years in which there may be no apprehension of arrest against the applicant by the police but he is avoiding the process of the court, therefore, he is not entitled for any relief.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, there appears no ground for grant of anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant.
Hence, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is, hereby, rejected.

However, it is directed that in case, the applicant appears and moves bail application before the learned court concerned, it will be heard and decided expeditiously as far as possible in the light of law as laid down in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another LL 2021 SC 550, decided by Hon'ble the Supreme Court.
